body:
TRUST-ROOT (touches a rails deny-path, so a distinct-provider cross-model approve is required before merge).

Follow-up to T-01KZW2DQKN5C1BANMMTTMPK8TS (PR #490, merged as e87c933d). That ticket taught the ungated-tool spoof branch to see target-keyed arguments and gave it a file-vs-directory distinction. Three defects in that distinction were found by cross-model review AFTER the merge window closed, and are fixed on branch `fix/opencode-rail-provenance-followup`. They share one root cause, which is the same one the merged ticket's handoff recorded: an existing classification is reused to answer a subtly different question.

Here the reused classification is the CALLER'S. The ungated branch exists precisely because the tool name and the argument shape are untrusted, and then it let that same untrusted argument shape decide whether ancestor detection applies.

=== DEFECT 1: aliased keys erase ambiguity ===

`spoofCandidates` deduplicates candidates by string but recorded provenance only for keys that asserted something. One path arriving under both an ambiguous and a file-specific key therefore kept only the file half. Measured on the merged revision with a ticket railing `assets.bundle/**`:

  {target: 'assets.bundle'}                          -> deny
  {target: 'assets.bundle', filePath: 'assets.bundle'} -> ALLOW

Adding a second spelling relaxed the check. In this branch the arg shape is exactly what a spoofing caller controls, so provenance must merge conservatively: any ambiguous occurrence revokes a file assertion made about the same path, the way an explicit directory key already overrides one.

=== DEFECT 2: a claimed file shed EVERY ancestor form ===

A target the caller named with a file-specific key was passed to `railHit` with `ancestors: false`, which switches off ancestor detection wholesale. That is right for the form the merged ticket's requirement 3 targeted -- `src/index.mjs` reading as an ancestor of `src/**/test/*.mjs`, an over-block created purely by the `**`. It is wrong for the form where the rail set itself contradicts the caller: a rail `assets.bundle/**` STATES that `assets.bundle` is a directory, so `{filePath: 'assets.bundle'}` was allowed to shed the check by asserting otherwise.

The fix is a middle setting rather than a widening or a narrowing. `railHit` gains `ancestors: 'literal'`, which keeps every ancestor form except the one an anchored `**` creates, and the ungated branch passes it for a claimed file. Deciding this from the frozen rails rather than from the argument key also settles a contradiction two consecutive review rounds produced, one asking for the key to be trusted more and the next for it to be trusted less.

Requiring a successful stat instead does not work here: an absent target is the normal case for a file a tool is about to create, so a stat requirement re-introduces the over-block requirement 3 was written to remove.

=== DEFECT 3: padded spellings are not the same path ===

Candidate extraction rejects a blank value with `trim()` but stores the raw string, and `railHit` then canonicalizes only that raw form. A padded ` test/frozen.test.mjs ` resolves to a different lexical path and misses the rail, while any tool that normalizes its input acts on the frozen one.

This one is NOT confined to the ungated branch. Measured on the merged revision with a ticket railing `test/**`:

  task  {target: ' test/frozen.test.mjs '}    -> ALLOW
  write {filePath: ' test/frozen.test.mjs '}  -> ALLOW

The second is the mutating branch, which does write files. It is fixed inside `railHit`, where the ungated, mutating, shell, and gate-argv call sites all pass through, rather than at any one of them.

=== BEHAVIOUR THIS CHANGE LEAVES AS IT IS ===

The extension heuristic in `namesAFile` keeps its current contract. A file-specific key licenses it; it is not authoritative on its own, because `filePath` is a key plenty of tools hand a directory. An absent `{targetFile: 'src/Makefile'}` therefore keeps ancestor detection and can be over-denied under an interior-wildcard rail. That is a deliberate trade-off, pinned by a test as a decision: this predicate gates only tools that never write files, and a visible refusal there is cheaper than a miss.

Three further surfaces are unchanged, each for a stated reason: the mutating branch's `singleFile` semantics (a known structured mutator writes the one file it names, so ancestor detection is genuinely the wrong question there); the sibling pi/codex adapters; the CI diff gate, which remains the unbypassable backstop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ungated tool naming a path under BOTH an ambiguous and a file-specific key is denied when the ambiguous reading hits a rail, in both property orders. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- `{filePath: <a rail's parent directory>}` is denied: a rail `assets.bundle/**` states that `assets.bundle` is a directory, and the rails outrank the key. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- A concrete non-rail file under an interior-wildcard rail is still allowed, so requirement 3 of the merged ticket does not regress. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- `targetIsRailAncestor` keeps its full-ancestor contract for two-argument callers, and its narrowed form drops ONLY the anchored-`**` case -- an interior single-star ancestor still hits. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- A padded target is denied on the ungated branch AND on the mutating branch, which is the one that writes. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- The tests bite: each of the three defects is ALLOWED on the merged revision e87c933d and denied here, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- The existing OpenCode rail and handoff contracts pass unmodified. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs && git diff --quiet origin/main -- plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The integrations page states which side wins when a caller's key and the rail set disagree, so an operator can predict a denial. verify: `rg -q 'rail set' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/opencode.mdx`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`
- Trust-root tier: a distinct-provider cross-model approve is recorded before merge. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main --author-provider anthropic`

allow-suppression: none

=== RAILS NOTE ===

`plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs` and `plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs` are deliberately NOT railed: both must change. `plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs` is frozen, for the same reason the merged ticket froze it -- the deny-set is always-on artifact protection and must not become coupled to per-ticket rail policy.
title: opencode: the frozen rail set must outrank a caller's claim about a target
